# Admin Ops catalog — recurring chores → portal actions

**Purpose.** The owner has been running most day-to-day operations by asking an AI session to do them by hand (SSH, `qm`, `iptables`, SQL, Cloudflare). This catalog lists every *recurring operational chore* found in that history, how it was done manually, and how it now works (or should work) as a hard-coded, audited action in the admin portal (`/admin/ops/**`, `lib/admin-ops/*`, `worker/admin-ops.ts`).

**Source.** Mined 2026-10-01 from every owner message in `/root/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` (3,163 user messages → 2,840 after de-duplication; tool results and system text excluded), cross-checked against `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` and `git log`. Frequencies are counts of distinct owner messages matching the chore (keyword match + manual reading), July 23 – Oct 1 2026. They undercount: one "fix this customer" message usually expanded into many manual steps.

**Legend.** ✅ shipped in this branch · 🟡 partial / wraps an existing action · 🔜 not built (reason given) · 🔗 owned by another workstream.

| # | Chore | Freq. | Status |
|---|-------|-------|--------|
| 1 | "Customer can't connect" / "is X healthy?" — diagnose a server | ~34 | ✅ Diagnose |
| 2 | Restart / reboot / start / stop a VM | ~32 | ✅ (existing power + Diagnose fixes + bulk) |
| 3 | Assign / transfer / reassign a dedicated IP | ~28 | ✅ same-node; 🔗 cross-node |
| 4 | Draft a ticket reply after investigating | ~26 | 🔜 (stays AI; Diagnose output is the evidence) |
| 5 | Renewal price / billing correction (grandfather, add-ons, renew now) | ~20 | 🟡 links to existing tools; 🔗 BILL |
| 6 | Migrate a server to another node (incl. keep IP) | ~16 | 🔗 VM move engine (stub wired) |
| 7 | Stuck / slow job, "it's stuck", queue too slow | ~16 | ✅ Job queue manager |
| 8 | DNS / custom-domain / subdomain not resolving | ~15 | ✅ Diagnose DNS + one-click resync |
| 9 | Grant free server / credit / extend trial | ~14 | ✅ credit/extend/free; 🔗 game-server grant (C) |
| 10 | Resize RAM/storage for a customer at no charge | ~12 | 🔜 (existing resize/disk flows; needs a "comp" flag) |
| 11 | Tear down test VMs / "did you destroy the test VMs?" | ~11 | ✅ Bulk delete (test accounts only) + orphan cleanup |
| 12 | Refund (wallet / card) | ~10 | ✅ wraps `refundPayment` |
| 13 | Root password / SSH access problems | ~9 | ✅ Diagnose (SSH check) + guest `sshd`; reset stays existing |
| 14 | Node health / "what's using resources" / node slow | ~7 | ✅ Diagnose node load + guest top + drain planner |
| 15 | Orphan IPs / "do we have free IPs?" | ~6 | ✅ Drift scan + safe release |
| 16 | Check logs to see what a user/server did | ~5 | ✅ Guest tools (journal, docker logs, game logs) |
| 17 | Transfer a server to another account | ~3 | ✅ Transfer |
| 18 | Deploy a server on a customer's account for free (N days) | ~3 | 🔗 C (partner game-server grants) / existing Grant VPS |
| 19 | DB ↔ Proxmox drift, orphan VMIDs, template presence | ~5 | ✅ Drift scan |
| 20 | Bulk actions across many servers | (implied by 2/11) | ✅ Bulk with concurrency |
| 21 | Node drain / rebalance before maintenance or when hot | ~6 | ✅ planner; 🔗 execution |
| 22 | Fix NAT / port forwards ("fix the port forwarding gap") | ~6 | ✅ Diagnose NAT check + resync |
| 23 | Restart the game container without touching the VM | ~8 | ✅ Restart game service |
| 24 | Resend an email (deployed/password/partner invite) | ~4 | 🔜 (EmailLog resend belongs to B adminmail) |
| 25 | Revoke / reissue SSL | ~3 | 🔜 (existing SSL_ISSUE flow; low frequency) |
| 26 | Apply Proxmox ACL role / token to nodes | ~2 | 🔜 (Q nodedocs: onboarding scripts) |

---

## 1. Diagnose a server ("can't connect", "is it healthy?") — ✅

**Frequency:** the single most common request (~34 direct, plus most ticket investigations). Representative: *"customer said they pointed their domain here but its not working"* (08-30), *"cant connect to this minecraft server cmuo7ajqt0rpohl44gj8triev"* (10-01), *"he says he still cannot connect, please do a deep audit"* (09-23), *"is everything running healthy after the reboot?"* (09-13).

**Manual procedure (AI):** look up the row in Postgres → `qm status` / Proxmox API on the right node → guest agent ping → SSH in (password or management key) → `systemctl status <game>`, `docker ps`, `ss -lntup`, `journalctl` → `iptables -t nat -S NXEON_FWD` on the owning node (or via the node agent) → `nc`/probe from outside → `dig` A/SRV → check recent jobs → explain. Typically 10–30 tool calls and a few minutes per ticket.

**Portal:** `/admin/ops/servers/<id>` → **Diagnose** (also embeddable via `ServerOpsPanel`). One ADMIN_OPS job gathers, in the worker:
- DB row + last 7 days of jobs (in-flight + failures), provision error/step;
- node API reachability, node CPU/RAM;
- VM existence on the recorded node, power state, uptime, CPU/RAM, `ipconfig0` vs `Server.ipAddress`, guest-agent ping;
- the server's expected DNAT rules (same `planNatRules` the real sync uses) vs the node's live chain (local iptables on the primary, node agent elsewhere);
- guest over SSH: load, RAM, root disk, failed units, OOM kills (24h), game unit + `is-active`, container restart count, last 80 journal lines → highlighted errors;
- join port bound inside the guest (any netns, same `gamePortBoundInGuest` provisioning uses);
- outside probe of SSH (banner) and the join port (TCP connect / UDP with in-guest confirmation) on the public address; flagged as *hairpin* when probing a primary-hosted server from the primary itself;
- subdomain A/SRV via public resolvers (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) vs `resolveGameServerDnsTarget`; customer's own domain A record.

`lib/admin-ops/diagnose-rules.ts` (pure, unit-tested) turns that into a verdict (healthy / degraded / down / unknown), a headline, **ranked probable causes with evidence**, the raw checks, and **one-click fixes** through existing paths: start/reboot (`serverAction`), reconcile (`reconcileServerFromProxmox`), restart game service (`gamePower`), NAT re-sync (`SYNC_FORWARDS`), DNS re-sync (`SYNC_GAME_DNS`), retry provisioning (`retryProvision`), open the job queue, open guest logs. When everything is green the headline gives the exact connect address and says the problem is client-side.

**Not covered / limits:** a true probe *from another node* needs a probe endpoint on the node agent (follow-up); today the outside probe runs from the primary. Per-server firewall rules are not yet evaluated rule-by-rule (the `blocked_path` cause points at them).

## 2. Power: restart / reboot / start / stop — ✅

**Freq.** ~32 (*"go ahead and restart it"*, *"reboot it"*, *"turn the free mc server back on on node 2"*, *"stop this vm, hes overdue"*, *"all servers need to be booted back up … if there is ever a restart"*).
**Manual:** `qm start/stop/reboot <vmid>` on the right node, or a DB-inserted job.
**Portal:** existing Start/Stop/Reboot on the server page (unchanged), Diagnose fixes, and **Bulk actions** (`/admin/ops/fleet`) with a concurrency cap (1–8, default 2) — the worker's `bulk_power` op releases the next server only when one finishes, skips (and reports) ineligible servers, persists progress so a worker restart resumes. "Boot everything after a node reboot" = Bulk → Start on all STOPPED servers of that node.

## 3. Dedicated IP: assign / reassign / release — ✅ (same node) · 🔗 cross-node

**Freq.** ~28 (*"assign the IP"*, *"give me a dedicated ip from the singapore pool"*, *"assign them both dedicated IPv4 address"*, *"just do the fucking transfer… is it attached to his server now"*, *"the IPv4 assigned to the node three test server was just a test IP … take that IPV4 and bring it over"*).
**Manual:** pick a FREE pool row, OVH/Hetzner vMAC, `qm set --net0 … --ipconfig0 …`, power-cycle, fix `Server.ipAddress/sshPort`, NAT resync, DNS resync, tell the customer. The older admin "release IP" button only freed the DB row and left the VM configured with the address.
**Portal (IP & placement card):**
- **Give IP to another server (same node)** — dry-run plan + warnings (downtime, billing), typed confirmation (the IP), reason. Worker `ip_reassign`: stop source → release (vMAC removed) → source onto NAT (new private IP + SSH port + game join forwards) → claim *that exact address* for the target (`allocateDedicatedIp(..., { preferAddress })`) → net0/ipconfig0 → power-cycle → restart source → NAT + DNS resync → notify both owners. The target is held by a HOLD job so nothing else runs on it meanwhile. Never auto-retried; each step idempotent.
- **Release IP (→ NAT)** — the correct version of the old release button.
- **Assign a pool IP** — first free or a specific FREE address on the node; checkbox for whether the add-on is billed at renewal.
- **Move to another node** — calls `requestVmMove` (stub until `feature/vm-node-migration` lands — that branch owns cross-node moves and IP carry-over).

## 4. Ticket replies — 🔜 (stays with AI)

**Freq.** ~26 (*"draft me a reply"*, *"give me ticket reply"*). Memory rule: never send without sign-off. This is language work, not an operation; the Diagnose result (headline, connect address, evidence) is the factual input a human or AI uses to write it. Canned replies already exist.

## 5. Renewal price / billing corrections — 🟡 · 🔗 BILL

**Freq.** ~20 (grandfathered price, add-on totals, "renew now", "his renewal price should be $8.99, next month 20% off"). Existing tools on the server page (grandfather price form, Renew now, Extend). The ops console links there and adds credit/refund/extend with reason + notification. Stripe/renewal internals are owned by the BILL workstream; nothing here edits `lib/stripe.ts` / `worker/billing.ts`.

## 6. Migrate a server to another node — 🔗

**Freq.** ~16 (*"migrate their server to node 4 … services, port forwards, dbs, files"*, *"move this customer's entire server onto node 3"*, *"migrate the free mc server to node 2 … porting, sub domains, DNS"*). Owned by the VM move engine branch. The ops console exposes it via `requestVmMove({serverId, targetNodeId, dryRun, reason})` (single server and from the drain planner); today it returns "engine not merged".

## 7. Stuck / failed jobs — ✅

**Freq.** ~16 (*"this apply game server settings stuff is stuck"*, *"im pretty sure its stuck, please wake it up"*, *"run the cleanup and restart the worker"*).
**Manual:** SQL on `Job`, sometimes restarting the worker.
**Portal:** `/admin/ops/jobs` — Active / Stuck / Failed / All views, per-server filter, live refresh. Re-queue (FAILED only), Cancel (QUEUED only), Force-fail (RUNNING only after 30 silent minutes) — each with a reason, compare-and-swap on the status, audit row. Policy (`lib/admin-ops/job-queue.ts`, tested): money-bearing jobs (RESIZE, DISK_EXPAND, ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP) are never re-queueable (their failure is refunded); PROVISION goes through Retry provisioning; cancelling a DELETE un-strands the server (ERROR + note → Reconcile).

## 8. DNS / subdomain / custom domain — ✅

**Freq.** ~15. Diagnose compares public DNS to the expected target and offers **Re-sync subdomain DNS**; a customer-domain mismatch is flagged *customer-side* with the right value to give them (and the NAT caveat that a bare domain can't carry a port).

## 9. Free server / credit / extend — ✅ · 🔗

**Freq.** ~14 (*"apply the credit and send it"*, *"extend his trial by a day"*, *"Give Thorabin a Terraria Server… free for 30 days"*).
**Portal (Customer ops card, `/admin/ops/customers`):** wallet credit/debit (wraps `adjustBalance`), extend/shorten term (wraps `adminExtendServer` — gifted days never prorate into refundable credit), make free/paid (wraps `adminSetServerFree`). Reason mandatory; optional in-app notification and/or email (generic notification template). Granting a *game* server on a chosen node for N days is the partner-grant workstream (C); VPS grants stay at `/admin/grant`.

## 10. Comp resource upgrades — 🔜

Existing resize/disk-expand flows charge the customer; a "comp" (no-charge, renewal unchanged until next term) option needs a money-path change owned by BILL. Logged as follow-up.

## 11. Tear down test VMs — ✅

**Freq.** ~11 (*"tear these down minecraft-o3nu1n, minecraft-nsrtzj"*, *"Yes, destroy all 3"*, *"are you tearing down the old game test servers?"*).
**Portal:** Bulk → Delete, fenced to servers owned by staff accounts or accounts excluded from revenue (the owner's/test accounts); typed `DELETE <n>`. Leftover VMs without rows are handled by the drift scan's orphan cleanup.

## 12. Refunds — ✅ (wraps `refundPayment`; card when traceable, else wallet).

## 13. SSH / root password — ✅ diagnose · existing reset

**Freq.** ~9 (*"I reset their root password… now it says I can't connect"*, *"is the ssh password the same?"*). Diagnose shows whether the *platform* can log in and whether sshd answers from outside; guest tool **SSH daemon** shows sshd state + recent auth failures. The owner explicitly does not want passwords reset as an automatic fix, so it is never suggested; the existing reset button remains on the server page.

## 14. Node health / resources — ✅

**Freq.** ~7 (*"what server is using the most resources"*, *"primary node is becoming unresponsive"*). Diagnose reports node CPU/RAM; guest tools **Top processes (CPU/RAM)**, **Largest files**, **Disk usage**; the drain planner shows committed-RAM % per node before/after.

## 15/19. Orphans, drift, templates — ✅

**Freq.** ~11 combined (*"do we have any free IPs that aren't being used by deleted or expired servers?"*, *"all ips that become orphaned need to be auto released to the pool"*, VMID reuse incidents).
**Portal:** `/admin/ops/fleet` → **Run drift scan** (worker `drift_scan`, read-only): orphan VMs (prod-tagged, no row — staging and untagged infra VMs never flagged), unmanaged VMs (info), missing VM, VM on the wrong node, DB-vs-Proxmox status mismatch, stranded PENDING/PROVISIONING/DELETING rows with no job, duplicate vmids across nodes, IP pool orphans/conflicts/mismatches, missing templates per provisioning node. Safe fixes only: destroy a **stopped** orphan (typed vmid; worker re-verifies tag/state/no row; `destroyVmIdempotent`), release an orphaned IP (refused if any server holds the address or a live DNAT targets it), reconcile status, diagnose.

## 16. Logs — ✅ Guest tools: service journal, container logs, game unit status, cloud-init, kernel OOM.

## 17. Transfer a server to another account — ✅

Moves Server + volumes, websites, DBs, apps, cron, SSL to the new owner; invoices/history stay; optional root-password rotation; typed hostname confirmation; both owners notified.

## 21. Node drain / rebalance — ✅ planner · 🔗 execution

Pick a node → plan (drain fully or down to a committed-RAM target, same region first, 10 % headroom, largest first, dedicated-IP servers flagged) → "Stop new provisions" toggle (existing `setNodeAcceptsProvisions`) → per-move button calls the VM move engine.

## 22/23. NAT gaps, restart game container — ✅ (Diagnose NAT check + resync; **Restart game service** = existing GAME_POWER, VM untouched).

## 24–26. Resend emails, SSL reissue, Proxmox ACL — 🔜

Low frequency and owned elsewhere (B adminmail owns EmailLog; SSL has its own flow; node ACLs live in Q's onboarding scripts).

---

## Safety model (applies to every action above)

- `requireArea("fleet")` (ADMIN) for server/fleet ops, `requireArea("billing")` for money ops; refused while impersonating. Proven structurally by `test/admin-ops-actions-guards.test.ts`.
- Mandatory reason (4–300 chars) on every mutating op, written to `AuditLog` alongside the admin id and target.
- Destructive ops require a typed confirmation checked **server-side** (IP address, vmid, hostname, `ACTION <n>`).
- Remote work only in the root worker (`ADMIN_OPS` jobs); the web process never mutates Proxmox/iptables.
- Read-only ops (diagnose, guest commands, drift) never block on a wedged server job and run in parallel (`adminOpsLockKey`).
- Guest commands are a fixed whitelist with allowlisted, single-quoted parameters; output capped at 64 KB and scrubbed of the root password.
- Mutating ops are not auto-retried; each step is idempotent and re-runnable after a Diagnose.
- SANDBOX (`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`): diagnose returns a labelled simulation, IP ops swap DB rows only, destroys are no-ops.

# Part VII — Change history

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:
   git log --date=short --pretty='%h|%ad|%s'
   git blame <file> -L <start>,<end>
```

## Session log — 2026-07-26 into 2026-07-27 (the customer-readiness push)
the panel's Files feature timed out, and firewall sync retried 3× and failed to authenticate — both
against a server the customer insisted had a working, reachable management key.

- **Root cause, fully verified before touching anything**: `connectionTarget()` (`lib/sftp.ts`) has
  always hardcoded port 22 for ANY server with a dedicated IP, ignoring `Server.sshPort` entirely for
  that branch (that field is the NAT-mapped *external* port for non-dedicated servers — a different,
  `@unique` concept, not safe to reuse here). `nc -zv <ip> 22` timed out; `nc -zv <ip> 2222` succeeded;
  connecting directly with the server's own stored management key on `:2222` worked immediately
  (`sshd -T` confirmed `port 2222`). So the management key and the connection plumbing were both fine
  — the platform was just always dialing the wrong port for this one server.
- **Fix**: new nullable `Server.guestSshPort` column (additive, `db push`'d — changes nothing for any
  existing server, since `null` falls back to `?? 22`, today's exact behavior). `connectionTarget()`'s
  dedicated-IP branch now reads `server.guestSshPort ?? 22` instead of a bare `22`. Selected into
  `lib/actions-files.ts`'s server query (the Files feature); `worker/firewall.ts` already `include`s
  the whole row so it picked it up for free. New unit tests in `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`
  pin both the override and the (unchanged) default. Admin server detail page now shows "Guest SSH
  port override" for any server with a dedicated IP, so this doesn't stay a hidden DB-only field.
- **The firewall side needed a second, separate finding**: even with the port fixed, `syncFirewall`
  would still fail — this guest's `iptables` (legacy) returns "Incompatible with this kernel" (likely
  1Panel's own nftables-only setup). Checked the LIVE guest directly: `iptables -L INPUT` showed only
  UFW's own chains (`ufw-before-input` etc.), policy DROP — confirming the platform's `NXEON_FW` chain
  has in fact never once been successfully applied to this guest, so there was nothing live to
  "detach". The customer's 6 stale `FirewallRule` DB rows are display-only leftovers; deleting them
  requires no guest-side sync (and syncing them now would risk appending a default-DROP that doesn't
  know about port 2222 — `FW_KEEP_OPEN_TCP_PORTS` only keeps 22 open — so deliberately did NOT trigger
  a sync). `SYNC_FIREWALL` jobs are only ever created by `lib/actions-firewall.ts` on an explicit rule
  edit (confirmed — no periodic/cron trigger exists), so once those 6 rows are gone, nothing re-fires
  on its own.
- **Not yet done**: deleting the 6 stale `FirewallRule` rows was blocked by the auto-mode permission
  classifier ("Modify Shared Resources") on a direct DB write — needs the owner to run it or grant it.
  Worth a platform-wide follow-up too: any guest running an nftables-only setup (1Panel defaults to
  this) can never successfully use the panel firewall feature at all, independent of this port issue.

**Files:** `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/sftp.ts`, `lib/actions-files.ts`,
`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`.

  never reported as failure. Fixes go through existing paths only.

  is released only if no server holds it and no live DNAT targets it. Bulk start/stop/reboot/game
  restart/delete with a 1–8 concurrency cap (delete fenced to staff/test accounts). Drain/rebalance
  planner (same region first, committed RAM, 10% headroom).
- **Job queue manager**: requeue (FAILED; never RESIZE/DISK_EXPAND/ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP — refunded on

  server's expected DNAT rules vs the node's live chain, guest load/RAM/disk/failed units/OOM/game
  unit/container restarts/log highlights over SSH, join port bound in the guest, outside probe of SSH
  and the join port, subdomain A/SRV and the customer's own domain via public resolvers. Unknown is
  never reported as failure. Fixes go through existing paths only.
- **IP ops (same node)**: reassign a dedicated IP between two servers (source → NAT with fresh NAT IP,
  SSH port and game join forwards; exact address claimed for the target via a new optional
  `preferAddress` on `allocateDedicatedIp`; target held by a HOLD job meanwhile), release to NAT
  (fixes the old release button that freed the DB row but left the VM on the address), assign from
  the pool (billable flag). Cross-node goes to `requestVmMove` (stub).
- **Fleet**: drift scan (orphan/unmanaged/missing/misplaced VMs, status mismatches, stranded rows,
  duplicate vmids, IP pool orphans/conflicts, missing templates) with safe cleanup — a stopped,
  prod-tagged, row-less VM can be destroyed after a typed vmid and a run-time re-check; an orphaned IP
  is released only if no server holds it and no live DNAT targets it. Bulk start/stop/reboot/game
  restart/delete with a 1–8 concurrency cap (delete fenced to staff/test accounts). Drain/rebalance
  planner (same region first, committed RAM, 10% headroom).
- **Job queue manager**: requeue (FAILED; never RESIZE/DISK_EXPAND/ASSIGN_DEDICATED_IP — refunded on
  failure — nor PROVISION), cancel (QUEUED), force-fail (RUNNING after 30 silent minutes); CAS on
  status; a cancelled DELETE un-strands the server.
- **Guest ops**: restart game service (existing GAME_POWER), and 16 whitelisted read-only diagnostic
  commands with typed, allowlisted parameters (`lib/admin-ops/guest-commands.ts`) — no free shell;
  output capped at 64 KB and scrubbed.
- **Customer ops**: credit/debit, refund, extend/shorten, make free/paid (all wrapping the existing
  money actions), transfer a server to another account (server + volumes/websites/DBs/apps/cron/SSL;
  optional root-password rotation) — mandatory reason, optional in-app notification/email.
- **Schema**: `JobType.ADMIN_OPS` (additive enum value). **Hook-ups outside the module**:
  `worker/index.ts` (import, `ADMIN_OPS: adminOps` in the handler map, `adminOpsLockKey` in
  `lockKeyFor`), `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` (`opts.preferAddress`), `lib/admin-groups.ts` (nav tab).
- **Tests**: `test/admin-ops-logic.test.ts` (diagnose rules, guest whitelist, job policy, drift, drain,

  opens with `gate()` = requireArea + not-impersonating; typed confirmations enforced server-side).

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

A2 adminops report. This is incomplete: the console UI was never rendered (no dev server, no Playwright run), and the final test and typecheck re-run after my last fix has not happened. Everything is committed and pushed.

**Branch / worktree:** `feature/admin-ops-actions` in `/opt/nxeon-wt-adminops`. Commits `db52dafe77` (the console) and `7180b7c0c7` (one bug fix plus test typing). Progress note: `/root/agent-notes/adminops.md`.

**Step 1, mining the history:** I read all 3,163 of the owner's messages (2,840 after removing duplicates) and wrote `docs/ADMIN-OPS-CATALOG.md`. It lists 26 recurring chores with how often each came up, how it was done by hand, how it now works in the portal, and its status. The most common: diagnosing "customer can't connect" (~34), power actions (~32), dedicated-IP assign/reassign (~28), ticket replies (~26, left to a human or AI), billing and renewal fixes (~20).

**Step 2, what was built:**
- **Code:** `lib/admin-ops/*` holds the pure logic, the server actions and the VM-move stub. `worker/admin-ops.ts` runs the new `ADMIN_OPS` job type. `components/admin/ops/*` holds the panels, including the embeddable `ServerOpsPanel`. The pages are `app/admin/ops/{,servers,servers/[id],jobs,fleet,customers}`.
- **Diagnose:** one click runs, in the worker, the checks you listed (VM state, guest agent, game service and container, port in guest, DNAT on the node, outside probe, DNS, logs, resources, recent jobs). It returns a verdict, ranked probable causes with evidence, and one-click fixes that go through the existing actions. A check that couldn't run counts as unknown, never as a failure.
- **IP ops (same node only):** reassign a dedicated IP between two servers, release one back to NAT, or assign one from the pool. Each shows a dry-run preview first; reassign and release also need the IP typed to confirm. The other server is held by a placeholder job so nothing else runs on it during a reassign. These ops never retry automatically.
- **Moving between nodes:** goes only through `requestVmMove`, which is a stub until PM's engine is merged. I built no move logic of my own.
- **Fleet:** a DB-vs-Proxmox drift scan with safe cleanup (only stopped, production-tagged VMs with no DB row can be destroyed; an IP is released only if nothing uses it), bulk power with a concurrency limit of 1–8 (bulk delete only for staff/test accounts), and a drain/rebalance planner that plans but doesn't execute.
- **Job queue:** requeue, cancel and force-fail, each with a reason. Money-bearing job types and PROVISION can't be re-queued, because failed money jobs are already refunded.
- **Customer ops:** credit, refund, extend, make free and transfer server, with a reason and an optional notification. Money paths wrap the existing actions (`adjustBalance`, `refundPayment`, `adminExtendServer`, `adminSetServerFree`); nothing in BILL's Stripe or billing files was edited.
- **Guest ops:** restart the game service through the existing GAME_POWER job, plus 16 whitelisted read-only diagnostic commands with captured output. There is no free shell.

**Verification:**
- Unit tests in `test/admin-ops-logic.test.ts` and `test/admin-ops-actions-guards.test.ts`: 32 of 33 passed. The one failure was a real bug (the default "/" path was rejected) and is fixed but not re-run.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the whole tree showed only two test typing errors, now fixed but not re-run.
- A sandbox end-to-end run of the job executor against my throwaway DB passed: diagnose, rejecting a hostile command, IP reassign with correct DB state afterwards (old server moved to NAT; the IP now on the target), release, drift scan with orphan-IP cleanup, refusing to destroy a VM that has a server row, and fencing bulk delete.

**Schema:** one new `JobType` value, `ADMIN_OPS` (additive), pushed only to the throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_adminops`.

**Files edited outside my area:**
- `worker/index.ts`: an import, `ADMIN_OPS: adminOps` in the handler map, and `adminOpsLockKey(j)` added to `lockKeyFor` (D1 owns this file).
- `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`: an optional `opts.preferAddress` parameter on `allocateDedicatedIp`.
- `lib/admin-groups.ts`: an "Ops console" nav tab.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

**Integration points:**
- Drop `<ServerOpsPanel serverId={server.id} />` into `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`; I didn't touch that page.
- Replace the body of `requestVmMove` in `lib/admin-ops/vm-move.ts` when `feature/vm-node-migration` merges.

**Still to do:**
1. Re-run the tests and `tsc` (the command is in the note).
2. Render the UI on port 3107 with Playwright at mobile and desktop widths, then `rm -rf .next`.
3. Drop the throwaway DB and role, and remove the untracked `.env`.

**Risks and follow-ups:**
- The "outside" probe runs from the primary, so for servers on the primary it is a hairpin test. A true probe from another node needs a probe endpoint on the node agent.
- If the worker restarts mid-reassign, the source and target can be left half-moved. Each step is idempotent, so the fix is to run Diagnose on both and re-run the reassign.
- Not built: no-charge resource upgrades (BILL's money path), resending emails (B), and granting a game server on a chosen node (C).
- Commit messages carry the brief's `Co-Authored-By: Claude` line rather than the Opus 5.5 attribution.
- I ran no seed scripts and wrote nothing to `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`; my sandbox script only touches the throwaway DB.
